newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen says offerings to cover beyond 1997.
newsitem.headline: Loewen says offerings to cover beyond 1997.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc said Monday that its US$1.0 billion shelf registration with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission should cover one to two years of financing.
Chief financial officer Paul Wagler also said in an interview that the debt and equity offerings would not have an impact on earnings forecasts.
"The earnings expectations remain unchanged," he said. Consensus forecasts are for the funeral home operator to earn around US$1.57 to US$1.58 a share this year.

The registration "certainly (will cover) beyond this year," Wagler said. Loewen Vice President of Finance Dwight Hawes said such shelf registrations were "supposed to represent about a two-year window."

The funds are likely to be used to finance Loewen's aggressive acquisition program. It has previously projected US$600 million to US$750 million in acquisitions in 1997. Last year Loewen raised about US$1.5 billion but that was a record that will not be repeated in 1997, Wagler said.
Loewen said the offerings would consist of debt and equity but that the proportions have not yet been allocated.
The past pattern at the company has been to raise twice as much debt as equity, Wagler said.
Loewen shares were down 0.15 to 45.50 in Toronto and unchanged at 33 in New York. Wagler said the announcement was in line with market expectations.
